# Named Routes

**Type-safe routes, URLs and assets for seven frameworks — with an integrated MCP server for AI agents.**

`@triooo/named-routes` · **v2.2.0** · [Documentation](docs/en/index.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [License](LICENSE)

<a id="overview"></a>
Named Routes discovers routes from your framework and generates a typed manifest. Reference routes by name rather than hard-coded paths, build URLs and asset links, and let your framework handle rendering and navigation. The runtime does not replace your router.

## What’s new in v2.2.0

- Explicit public URLs with `route.url(name, options)`; no positional placeholders.
- Opt-in semantic route names, source-file comments in generated manifests, and typed HTTP endpoint descriptors when static method discovery is available.
- Integrated read-only MCP, versioned LLM documentation, improved CLI packaging and bounded retries for transient Windows filesystem errors.
- Reorganized framework guides, root/subpath examples, translated release notes and website SEO.

Already available since v2.1.0: native Astro integration, typed assets and CDN URLs, asset versioning, `route.localize()`, `route.withQuery()`, `route.canonical()`, `route.alternates()`, `route.withDefaults()` and CLI audit.

<a id="installation"></a>
## Installation

Tooling requires Node.js 22.12+; exported types require TypeScript 5.4+. Choose your existing package manager. The commands below install the current published version; for an unpublished checkout, use a locally built tarball.

```sh
npm install @triooo/named-routes
# or
pnpm add @triooo/named-routes
```

[Installation](docs/en/topic-installation.md)

<a id="quick-start"></a>
## Quick start — Next.js

For example, create `src/app/users/[user]/page.tsx` in a Next.js App Router project. Configure the wrapper in `next.config.ts`.

```ts
import { withNamedRoutes } from "@triooo/named-routes/next";

export default withNamedRoutes({});
```

Start the dev server or generate the module. With the default `src/routes.generated.ts` output and `@/` mapped to `src/`, use the generated helper in a component. The name below assumes default path-based naming.

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";
import { route } from "@/routes.generated";

export function UserLink() {
  return <Link href={route("users.$user", { user: 42 })}>User 42</Link>;
}
```

Do not edit generated files. Configure stable aliases or naming conventions instead. Other frameworks have their own setup and navigation guides.

[Quick start — Next.js](docs/en/topic-quick-start.md)

## Public URLs and deployment paths

`route()` is intended for named route generation and native navigation; `route.url()` explicitly builds a public URL. These examples assume an existing Next.js generated route and its configured base.

### Without base path

```ts
route("users.$user", { user: 42 }); // /users/42
route.url("users.$user", { params: { user: 42 } }); // /users/42
```

### With base path `/app`

```ts
route("users.$user", { user: 42 }); // /users/42 (Next Link adds /app)
route.url("users.$user", { params: { user: 42 } }); // /app/users/42
```

In generated Astro, SvelteKit and manual projects, `route()` includes the configured navigation base by default in 2.2.0. Next.js, Nuxt, Vue Router, React Router and TanStack Router retain internal paths for their native routers. Use `route(name, params, { basePath: false })` when an internal path is required. Direct `createRoutes()` retains its existing default. Avoid double prefixes.

[basePath](docs/en/topic-base-path.md) · [route.url()](docs/en/topic-public-url.md)

<a id="ai-agents"></a>
## AI agents and MCP

The MCP server is included in the same npm package, not a separate package. With optional dependencies installed, it runs locally over stdio. It can consult the documentation and read an existing static generated route manifest; it does not execute project configuration or edit files.

```sh
pnpm exec named-routes mcp --help
pnpm exec named-routes-mcp --version
```

Verify the entry point locally. After v2.2.0 is published, the following client configuration can start the MCP server. Replace the root with your trusted project directory and merge the entry into your client’s existing configuration.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "named-routes": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@triooo/named-routes@2.2.0", "mcp", "--root", "C:/dev/my-app"]
    }
  }
}
```

Without `--root`, only documentation is available. Generate the manifest first for route inspection. Use `--manifest` for custom outputs (relative to the root). The server does not prove that the manifest is current or that a route is authorized or deployed. On Windows, see the direct Node launcher guide if npx shims fail.

## CLI

The CLI runs from the application directory. Use the scoped package name with npx, or the installed binary with pnpm exec. See the CLI reference for configuration, watch and migration options.

```sh
npx @triooo/named-routes list
pnpm exec named-routes generate
pnpm exec named-routes check
pnpm exec named-routes doctor
pnpm exec named-routes audit
```

[CLI](docs/en/topic-cli.md)

## Upgrading from 2.1.0

Review base-path behavior before upgrading, particularly if your Astro, SvelteKit or generated manual application already prefixes URLs. Remove duplicate prefixes or explicitly request internal paths. Semantic naming is opt-in. Regenerate your route module and run the consumer type checker.
